title: GET /risks/:riskId rejects a riskId that belongs to another organization
description: risk-register.routes.ts verifyRiskAccess() first calls verifyRiskOwnership(), which loads only { organizationId, projectId } and compares organizationId against request.user.organizationIdString before the service layer is ever invoked.
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) each with at least one risk
Valid JWT for a user in org A holding risk.read
steps: As an org A user, call GET /risks/:riskId using a riskId (or riskCode RISK-YYYY-NNNN) belonging to org B
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 'Access denied' — no risk name, score, or treatment data from org B is returned in the response body.

title: An org member who is not assigned to a risk's project is denied access to that risk even with risk.read
description: assertProjectAccess() (lib/project-access.ts) is invoked inside verifyRiskAccess() after the org-ownership check succeeds. It calls projectScopeClient.getScope() and rejects with 403 'You are not a member of this project' when the caller isn't in the risk's projectId — a second IDOR gate beyond organization membership.
preconditions: Org A has Project 1 and Project 2
A risk exists in Project 1 with a non-null projectId
User is a member of Project 2 only, holds risk.read at the org level
steps: As the Project-2-only user, call GET /risks/:riskId for the Project 1 risk
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 'You are not a member of this project' despite the user belonging to the same organization and holding risk.read.

title: PUT /risks/:riskId rejects a caller who lacks the risk.update permission
description: The route's preHandler chain runs augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant() then fastify.requirePermission('risk.update') before verifyRiskAccess() executes, so a permission-less caller is rejected before any risk data is touched.
preconditions: User authenticated with a valid JWT but no risk.update permission (org-level or project-granted)
steps: As the permission-less user, call PUT /risks/:riskId with a valid body changing the risk's name
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 before the update reaches RiskRegisterService.updateRisk(); the risk document is unchanged.

title: PUT /risks/:riskId/acceptance/approve rejects a caller who lacks the risk.approve permission
description: This route's preHandler requires risk.approve specifically (distinct from risk.update, which governs the /acceptance/request submission route) — a user who can submit an acceptance request must not automatically be able to decide one.
preconditions: Caller holds risk.update but not risk.approve
steps: As the risk.update-only user, call PUT /risks/:riskId/acceptance/approve with decision='approved'
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 before processAcceptanceDecision() runs; acceptance.status remains 'pending'.

title: Holding risk.approve does not let an attacker approve an acceptance request they were never named on
description: processAcceptanceDecision() (RiskRegisterService.ts:1341) checks existingRisk.acceptance.approvers.some(a => a.userId === user.userId) as a second gate after the risk.approve permission check passes. This is the deliberate authority-matrix control: the permission grants the *capability* to approve risks in general, but only the named approverIds on that specific request may exercise it — verifying an attacker can't bypass named-approver authority just by holding the org-wide permission.
preconditions: Risk has acceptance.status='pending' with approverIds=[UserA] only
UserB holds risk.approve at the org level but is not in approverIds
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 'You are not authorized to approve this request' even though UserB's JWT carries risk.approve — permission alone does not satisfy the named-approver authority check.

title: A requester can name themselves as the sole approver and self-approve their own acceptance request
description: submitAcceptanceRequest() places request.approverIds verbatim into acceptance.approvers with no check that the requester (user.userId) is excluded from the list, and processAcceptanceDecision()'s authority check only verifies list membership — it never compares the decider against the original requester. A user with both risk.update and risk.approve can submit a request naming themselves as approverIds[0], then immediately approve it, bypassing the four-eyes intent of the acceptance workflow. Documents the current gap for a product/security decision rather than asserting a fix already exists.
preconditions: User holds both risk.update and risk.approve
steps: As the user, POST /risks/:riskId/acceptance/request with approverIds=[self.userId] and a valid 50+ char justification
As the same user, PUT /risks/:riskId/acceptance/approve with decision='approved'
expectedResult: Current behavior: both calls succeed and acceptance.status becomes 'approved' with the requester as the sole recorded approver — no self-review/four-eyes prevention exists. Flagged for remediation (reject approverIds containing the requester's own userId, or block self-decision in processAcceptanceDecision).

title: Promote endpoint rejects a projectId in the request body that doesn't match the candidate module risk's actual project
description: ModuleRiskService.promote() (ModuleRiskService.ts:195) re-checks moduleRisk.projectId.toHexString() !== projectId after the route's own assertProjectAccess(body.projectId) passes — this stops an attacker who IS a member of some project P from promoting a module risk that actually belongs to project Q by simply supplying P in the request body. Without this second check, augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant + assertProjectAccess would only prove membership in the *claimed* project, not the *candidate's* real project.
preconditions: A pending module risk candidate belongs to Project Q
Caller holds risk.approve and is a member of Project P (not Q)
steps: POST /organizations/:orgId/module-risks/:id/promote with body { projectId: <Project P id> } where :id is the Project-Q candidate
expectedResult: Request fails with 409 'Candidate project does not match the requested project' — no risk entry is created in either project's register.

title: Promote and dismiss endpoints return 404 for a moduleRiskId belonging to another organization, not 403
description: Both ModuleRiskService.promote() and the dismiss route's getModuleRiskProjectId() filter the module-risks lookup by { _id, organizationId } together, so an org-B candidate id probed from org A never resolves to a document at all — preventing an attacker from distinguishing 'exists in another org' from 'doesn't exist' via response code, and closing off enumeration of cross-org module risk ids.
preconditions: Org B has a pending module risk candidate
Caller is an org A user with risk.approve
steps: As the org A user, POST /organizations/:orgAId/module-risks/:orgBCandidateId/promote with any valid projectId in the body
As the org A user, POST /organizations/:orgAId/module-risks/:orgBCandidateId/dismiss with a valid 10+ char reason
expectedResult: Both calls return 404 'Module risk not found' — the org-B candidate is never promoted or dismissed, and no information about its existence, project, or severity leaks in the response.
